class: ONE normalization — a word the digitization SUPPLIED to complete a phrase Migne prints defectively. Found while reading the plate for a different word on the same page, and invisible from the Latin alone by construction, because a completed phrase reads perfectly.

patches.find: id est Verbi Dei, id est ejusdem
patches.replace: id Verbi Dei, id est ejusdem
patches.why: the plate prints a bare 'id Verbi Dei' — no 'est' — and the contrast is on the same line, twice: 'id est ejusdem est scientiae cum Verbo' follows immediately with both forms spelled out. Read at 1200 dpi to be sure. Corpus Corporum supplied the copula, completing an elliptical phrase Migne left short. Same class as 8992's aemulatores leges→legis found this session and as 8948 convivum / 8990 concilio: the digitization does not only corrupt, it silently CORRECTS, and the corrected form reads perfectly, so nothing downstream can see it. ⚑ Also observed on the same line and deliberately NOT patched: the plate prints 'Verbo. Vel.' with a full stop where our transcription has 'Vel,'. A comma-for-period in the source transcription is a punctuation question across the whole corpus, not a single-site claim, and sweeping it is out of scope (Wilson's standing rule: ship new works, do not gold-plate). Recorded here so the observation is not lost.

confirmed_migne_no_patch: 1168A 'homo qui conve-|nientem habet cum omni creatura' — the plate prints CONVENIENTEM, hyphenated across the line, exactly as our file has it. The blind reader raised it because 'convenientem habet' occurs once in the whole corpus against 9 'convenientiam', and because the accusative has no head noun. NO patch: the corpus-frequency argument was good and the plate refutes it. The English renders the printed form; if anything it is a Pattern 18 question, not a transcription one.

1171D '*Homo* enim ubique discurrit' — the plate prints italic HOMO, exactly as our file. This was the blind reader's HIGHEST-value plate request and its hypothesis was sharp: *mobilis* stands in Sap 7:22, the gloss expounds mobility on both sides of the sentence, and *homo* is in neither the verse nor the argument — the 8990 alteration profile. NO patch. The argument was excellent and the plate says Homo.
